scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Sarah, 35, is healthy with no meaningful vision problems before the Mars mission.
key_measurements: VA 20/20 near and distance | Refraction 0.00 D | OCT peripapillary TRT = personal baseline | Fundus normal | No folds
charm_assessment: Baseline eye profile stored. All later eye results are compared with Sarah's own pre-flight values.
eye_tests_imaging: VA, cycloplegic refraction, fundus photography, OCT, ocular ultrasound, IOP.
immediate_action_steps: Store all results as Sarah's personal eye baseline.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Puffy face and head fullness typical of weightlessness. Vision unchanged.
key_measurements: VA 20/20 | Refraction 0.00 D | Delta TRT +8 µm | Cabin CO2 7-day average 2.4 mmHg
charm_assessment: Expected adaptation to the headward fluid shift. Fluid shift alone is not a SANS diagnosis.
checks_requested: Monthly vision self-test and symptom questions.
eye_tests_imaging: VA and Amsler grid self-test; scheduled OCT if in protocol.
immediate_action_steps: Continue normal duty; report any vision change.
equipment: VA chart, Amsler grid, C.H.A.R.M. tablet.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Sarah feels well and reports no vision change.
key_measurements: VA 20/20 | Refraction +0.25 D | Delta TRT +22 µm | No folds on OCT
charm_assessment: Early structural change without symptoms. Delta TRT has crossed NASA's earliest SANS indication (20 µm or more).
checks_requested: Repeat OCT to confirm the change; repeat refraction.
immediate_action_steps: Notify Crew Medical Officer; increase eye-test frequency; review cabin CO2 trend.
treatment_guidance: No treatment. Confirm the change is real and not scan noise.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Gradual blur when reading screens and small text up close. No pain.
key_measurements: Near VA reduced | Refraction +0.75 D (hyperopic shift) | Delta TRT +38 µm | Mild choroidal folds on OCT
charm_assessment: Two earliest-indication criteria now met (refractive shift of +0.75 D, chorioretinal folds) plus a rising Delta TRT trend. Suspected developing SANS.
checks_requested: Repeat VA and refraction; fundus photography; Amsler grid.
eye_tests_imaging: Refraction, near and distance VA, fundus, OCT with fold review.
immediate_action_steps: Provide adjustable or plus-power glasses; adjust screen text size; send images to Earth.
equipment: Spare and adjustable-focus glasses, fundus camera, OCT.
treatment_guidance: Optical correction only. Countermeasures only within an approved protocol.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Near reading clearly harder. Sarah still functions in her duties.
key_measurements: Delta TRT +58 µm | Frisén grade 1 disc edema on fundus | Posterior globe flattening on ocular ultrasound
charm_assessment: Clinically concerning optic disc edema (Delta TRT 55 µm or more, Frisén grade 1 or more) with globe flattening. Needs ophthalmology review.
eye_tests_imaging: Ultrasound for globe flattening; OCT; fundus (Frisén grade); IOP.
immediate_action_steps: Ophthalmology review (Earth); document findings; plan follow-up schedule.
treatment_guidance: Follow the mission SANS protocol. Measures to reduce the headward fluid shift (for example lower-body negative pressure, thigh cuffs) or keep CO2 low only within an approved research protocol. C.H.A.R.M. does not prescribe.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Mars communication delay makes real-time consultation with the Earth ophthalmologist impossible.
key_measurements: Eye results and images stored and queued for transmission to Earth.
charm_assessment: C.H.A.R.M. keeps the onboard SANS protocol, schedules repeat imaging and records every result until Earth review.
eye_tests_imaging: Repeat only what the onboard protocol requires.
immediate_action_steps: Open the onboard SANS protocol; continue step-by-step checks and recording.
equipment: C.H.A.R.M. tablet plus the same eye equipment.
treatment_guidance: Continue the plan already authorized for the mission.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Sudden vision loss, severe eye pain, double vision or new neurological symptoms at any stage.
key_measurements: Any of these symptoms reported in the daily check.
charm_assessment: Not attributed automatically to SANS. Treated as a possible eye or neurological emergency.
checks_requested: Immediate full eye and neurological check.
eye_tests_imaging: VA, pupils, fundus, ultrasound, IOP as available.
immediate_action_steps: Crew Medical Officer to Sarah immediately; urgent emergency protocol; contact Earth as soon as possible.
treatment_guidance: Emergency protocol. Do not wait for the SANS follow-up schedule.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Reads well with plus-power lenses. Mild difficulty with very small text.
key_measurements: Corrected near VA restored | Delta TRT +55 to +60 µm, not rising | Folds unchanged
charm_assessment: Changes established but not progressing. Correction restores function; close follow-up continues.
checks_requested: OCT and refraction at set intervals; monthly VA.
immediate_action_steps: Continue duty with correction; re-open alert if Delta TRT rises again.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
key_measurements: Refraction stable | Delta TRT stable or slowly falling | No new folds
charm_assessment: Stable SANS. Trend compared with every earlier scan; any new rise re-opens the alert.
checks_requested: OCT and refraction at set intervals; monthly VA.
immediate_action_steps: Continue duty with correction; re-open alert if Delta TRT rises again.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Sarah must be able to read displays and checklists during landing operations.
key_measurements: Corrected VA at task distance | Latest OCT and refraction
charm_assessment: Vision fitness for landing tasks confirmed with correction; post-landing eye follow-up planned.
checks_requested: Final in-flight eye check; post-landing exams.
eye_tests_imaging: VA, refraction, OCT, fundus, MRI if indicated on Earth.
immediate_action_steps: Confirm vision for landing tasks; schedule ophthalmology follow-up.
equipment: Onboard eye kit; Earth eye clinic.

scenario: Scenario 3: Vision changes during a Mars mission (SANS)
what_happens: Some changes improve within months; others may persist longer.
key_measurements: OCT, refraction and fundus at return and at follow-up visits
charm_assessment: Disc edema typically resolves about 3-12 months after return; follow-up until values approach baseline.
checks_requested: Final in-flight eye check; post-landing exams.
eye_tests_imaging: VA, refraction, OCT, fundus, MRI if indicated on Earth.
immediate_action_steps: Confirm vision for landing tasks; schedule ophthalmology follow-up.
equipment: Onboard eye kit; Earth eye clinic.
